questions.question: What features should boots or shoes have to protect a rider?

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they won't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What rule applies when you pass another vehicle?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish passing in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish passing in a legal passing zone.
You should honk your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish passing in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must happen only in areas where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
It requires you to speed up to keep with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space on all sides of your motorcycle gives you time and room to react safely if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead of you. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: You don't need to look over your shoulder if you check your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume other drivers will respond correctly to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when you are riding?

options.text: Your eyes only, not the rest of your face.
Your face only, not your eyes.
They are less effective than eyeglasses at protecting your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes only, not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses are not enough protection for either your eyes or face.

questions.question: How should you ride differently when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, start braking sooner, keep more space between vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps when entering traffic.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: Their combined effects can be stronger than using either alone.
They are less dangerous than using either alone.
The effects usually cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their combined effects can be stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, impair your ability to ride safely. Some drugs are even more dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your riding ability.
No, they usually don't affect your riding ability.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, over-the-counter drugs are always safe to take before riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your riding ability.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Understand the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. They tell you traffic rules. You must follow what these signs say.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps others see you at any time. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothes during the day too.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is in a crash, it should be:
questions.explanation: Always replace a helmet after a crash. It cannot protect you as well after impact.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check blind spots before changing lanes. This should be part of your regular checking routine.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather clothing gives the best protection to riders. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: When you ride with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume they have ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain everything.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain everything.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to stay safe. Never assume your passenger knows what to do. Give full instructions before every ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, a jacket should be worn:

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from sun and dehydration in hot weather.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after drinking one drink before riding:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drunk riding.
Means your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour on average. The time needed varies, so do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is safest?

options.text: It is unsafe because drivers cannot see turn signals.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and judge by eye.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. Looking at the tire is not enough because a soft tire may look normal.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in the lane?
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to change your position as conditions change.

questions.question: What does a plastic face shield protect you from?
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash. It also shields you from wind, dust, rain, insects, and rocks thrown up from other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have drunk too much. Take their keys if needed. Help them find another way home.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may need the lane.
You cannot see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle could block your escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during daylight. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing when riding to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What is allowed in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if no other vehicle is coming.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. Do not pass by riding off the main road either.

questions.question: What best reduces head or neck injury risk in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce head and neck injury risk in a crash.

questions.question: What kind of pants protect a motorcycle rider best?

options.text: Loose pants that flap in the wind.
Short pants that expose some leg.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or heavy synthetic material that cover your legs completely. They should fit snugly without flapping but allow you to move freely.
